newsitem.title: JAPAN: Most TOCOM precious metals rise, palladium lower.
newsitem.headline: Most TOCOM precious metals rise, palladium lower.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended mostly higher on Thursday, supported by the weakening of the yen, although palladium futures fell due to Russian PGM shipments looming on the horizon, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from 15 yen to 29 yen per gram higher. Benchmark April gold was up 25 yen at 1,268 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from one to eight yen per gram lower. Benchmark April was down two yen at 605 yen.
"Palladium prices are heading lower at a gradual pace, with Russian sales in sight. Concerns over Russia's ability to supply PGMs are also easing," one trader said.
On Wednesday, Almaz sources said Russia will ship about the same amount of PGMs this year as it did in 1996.
In gold futures, mixed trade was detected after a higher opening due to the yen's retreat.
The focus is still on the currency market, traders said.

"As spot gold is trapped within narrow ranges, direction hinges on the currency market," one trader said. "But private investors were tending to sell gold futures on price rallies as the dollar appears vulnerable to the downside."
Spot gold was quoted at $343.35/75 per ounce, up modestly from $342.70/343.20 in New York on Wednesday.
